fine_trace.note: The attacker-controlled XML string length determines the stack allocation size used for the parser copy.
For small XML, the parser copy is allocated as a dynamic stack buffer exactly large enough for the bytes and terminating NUL.
The unterminated element text is copied into the stack buffer with one trailing NUL byte at xml[len - 1].
Parsing begins on the attacker-controlled stack buffer and the parser records pi.str as this xml pointer.
After parsing a start tag with non-whitespace text, read_element calls read_text with pi->s pointing at attacker-controlled text content.
The text loop consumes bytes until it reads the terminating NUL and post-increments pi->s to one byte past the stack buffer object.

fine_trace.code: case '\0': set_error(&pi->err, "invalid format, document not terminated", pi->str, pi->s); return;
fine_trace.note: The error path passes the post-incremented pointer as current; the safety condition should keep current within the copied XML object instead of one byte past it.
The location formatter dereferences current before moving it backward, so the one-past-end pointer causes an out-of-bounds stack read.
